b

decision.explanation: By scalar multiplication, 18a·(b×c)=90, so a·(b×c)=5. Cyclic permutation preserves the scalar triple product, while swapping a and b reverses its sign. Thus c·(b×a)=-5.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
First, we factor out the constants and get

$$
\begin{aligned}3a\cdot (6b\times c) & =90 \\ 3\cdot 6\cdot [a\cdot (b\times c)] & =90 \\ a\cdot (b\times c) & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we swap $a$ and $c$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned}c\cdot (b\times a) & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
Remember that the scalar triple product $r\cdot (q\times p)$ is just the determinant of the matrix whose rows are given by $r,$ $q,$ and $p.$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot (q\times p) & =|\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =4\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|-1\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}|+(-2)\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =4((-2)\cdot 2-1\cdot 1)-(1\cdot 2-1\cdot 3)-2(1\cdot 1-(-2)\cdot 3) \\  & =-20+1-14 \\  & =-33.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: a·(b×c)=3(6)+5(-1)+(-4)(3)=1. Swapping a and c reverses the scalar triple product's sign, so c·(b×a)=-1.

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
First, we compute the triple scalar product 

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =⟨3,5,-4⟩\cdot ⟨6,-1,3⟩ \\  & =3\cdot 6+5\cdot (-1)+(-4)\cdot 3 \\  & =18-5-12 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we swap $a$ and $c$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned}c\cdot (b\times a)=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =⟨3,5,-4⟩\cdot ⟨6,-1,3⟩ \\  & =3\cdot 6+5\cdot (-1)+(-4)\cdot 3 \\  & =18-5-12 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}

Then, we swap $a$ and $c$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned}c\cdot (b\times a)=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 4
after.worked_solution:
Remember that the scalar triple product $a\cdot (b\times c)$ is just the determinant of the matrix whose rows are given by $a,$ $b,$ and $c.$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot |\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}|\,-\,(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}|\,+\,3\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\,(4\cdot 5-1\cdot 1)\,-\,(-1)\,(0\cdot 5-1\cdot (-2))\,+\,3\,(0\cdot 1-4\cdot (-2)) \\  & =2\,(19)\,-\,(-1)\,(2)\,+\,3\,(8) \\  & =38+2+24 \\  & =64.\end{aligned}
$$
